title: Skin tag removal
what: Soft growths on the skin are removed with radio waves, a laser, electric cautery, or freezing. Usually with local anesthetic.
why: If a skin tag bothers you, catches on clothes or jewelry, bleeds, or you do not like how it looks.
duration: usually 10 to 30 minutes, depending on how many
tell_doctor: A pacemaker. This matters for electric methods
If you tend to get raised, thick scars called keloids

prepare.title: Before removal
prepare.text: First, the doctor looks at the growths and decides how to remove them.

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: Do not tan for 2 weeks before and after. Do not put cream on the area on the day of the procedure.

bring: Your referral or the doctor's report
steps: The skin is cleaned with antiseptic
If needed, you get a numbing injection or numbing cream
The doctor removes the skin tags with the chosen method
A small wound or scab is left on the spot
Sometimes the tissue is sent to the lab for testing
feel: The numbing injection stings for a couple of seconds
During removal, you may feel warmth or notice a burning smell
after: Do not pick the scabs. They fall off on their own in 1 to 2 weeks
Keep the area clean and dry, as your doctor tells you
Protect the area from the sun for a few months, to avoid dark spots
red_flags: Bleeding that does not stop with pressure
Redness, swelling, pus, or a fever

faq.q: Can I tie off a skin tag with thread at home?
faq.a: Better not. You can get an infection, and no doctor checks the growth. It is safer to remove it at a clinic.
They can, especially where skin rubs. Removing old ones does not cause new ones.
